Subject: Handoff: EdgeWave integration — quick context + artifacts

Hi team,

Looping you in to pick up the implementation work for EdgeWave (deal EW-3821). Quick context:
- Use case: in-app content enrichment and search embeddings; expected bursty traffic during product launch (peak estimate: 5k reqs/min for first 3 hours).
- Tech stack: Node backend + Go microservices; they will call Redwood hosted endpoints initially, then migrate to a dedicated cluster in Q4.
- Compliance: need audit logs + customer-managed KMS on the dedicated migration.

Attachments (zipped): integration-samples.zip (includes sample SDK snippets, Postman collection), auth_config.yaml (their auth model), redwood-sla.pdf (SLA appendix).

As CSM I captured the go-live target window: July 12–14 (soft launch July 12). I recommended a canary ramp over 24–36 hours. Please review the samples and confirm the implementation plan below by EOD Monday:
- SDK bootstrap steps for Node and Go (see samples)
- Recommended retry/backoff and max concurrency settings for initial traffic surge
- A migration plan for switching from hosted to Dedicated (no downtime target)

Thanks — Monica

--
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Samir Rao <samir@edgewave.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: EdgeWave integration — traffic sentry & SDK fallbacks

Rishi — thanks, quick answers inline:
- Launch env: we'll point our staging namespace to Redwood hosted for smoke tests; production namespace will target hosted until we cut to Dedicated during the July 12–14 window.
- Token lengths: most calls are short (≈400–900 tokens), but search enrichment sometimes sends batches up to ~6k tokens. We'll flag anything >8k as we find it.

Two constraints from our side:
1) They want a client-side backoff not to exceed 45s between retries (we can cap exponential backoff jitter).
2) We require a deterministic retry policy in Node so we can replay failed requests in logs.

We'll review the node snippet tonight — question: do you recommend using the 'retry-after' header when present OR our capped exponential? We prefer deterministic behavior for replayability.

-Samir
EdgeWave Integrations

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Handoff: EdgeWave integration — traffic sentry & SDK fallbacks

Samir — quick guidance from infra/runtime side:
- Determinism vs retry-after: prefer deterministic (capped exponential with fixed jitter) for replayability, but honor 'retry-after' if it's within your cap (we recommend honoring it only if < 20s). If retry-after > 20s, treat as a long-window signal and surface as alert rather than waiting blindly.
- Circuit breaker: put an adaptive circuit breaker on 5xx/timeout errors. Trip threshold: 10 failures in 120s. Fail-open behavior: switch to a lower-capacity fallback model (cheaper variant) to preserve user experience while alerting SRE.
- Batching: for high-throughput search enrichment, use batching on your side (combine up to 8 items) and let Redwood handle efficient batching server-side; this reduces token overhead.
- Canary policy for hosted->dedicated migration:
  * Phase 1 (smoke): 1% traffic for 1 hour
  * Phase 2 (ramp): 10% for 2 hours, 50% next 3 hours, 100% on approval
- Observability hooks: add tracing header X-Request-ID and sample 1/100 traces with full payload to a secure S3 for evaluation.

Timeout/retry table (recommended):
- generation endpoints: timeout 120s, retries 4, base_backoff 300ms, max_backoff 30s, jitter 200-500ms
- embeddings endpoints: timeout 30s, retries 2, base_backoff 200ms, max_backoff 5s

I'll join the Monday sync to approve the runbook.

-Vivek
Director, Runtime & Infrastructure

- Canary schedule: we will carry out the Phase 1–Phase 4 ramp outlined by Vivek.

Rishi
